text:
alex: quick heads-up — saw a ~3x jump in request queue depth for spot-backed us-west1 pool around 02:12 UTC, tail latency spiking.
linda: same, interruptions on spot group g4dn-8x pretty high last night, a few pods OOM'ed during regen.
sam: do we have a single source of truth for the autoscaler config? wondering if scale-out threshold is too conservative for bursty chat traffic.
alex: it's in infra repo but the live cluster uses kustomize override. current policy is basically p95_latency > 300ms over 30s -> scale up by N, cooldown 10m. but Surge controls cap concurrent scale-ups to 2 to limit spot churn.
maria: I think the surge cap is the pain point — when interruptions happen we need more parallel launches to catch up, but that increases churn and cost.
tyler: suggestion: add a short-lived hedged warm pool (on-demand minimal fraction) to absorb sudden deltas, plus opportunistic spot fill for steady state.
sam: agree. Proposal: maintain hedge_pool_percent = 10% of desired capacity as on-demand (or reserved) and allow burst_surge up to 4 nodes for 60s if queue_depth delta > 50.
alex: here's a quick config sketch I had in mind:
```
autoscaler:
  metric: p95_latency
  scale_up_condition: p95_latency > 300ms for 30s OR queue_depth_inc > 50
  base_cooldown: 10m
  surge:
    burst_limit: 4
    burst_window: 60s
  hedge_pool_percent: 10
  interruption_smoothing: true
```
maria: want to add gradual backoff for repeated preemptions: if a node slot preempted twice in 30m, reduce allocation share for that AZ by 30% for 15m.
linda: +1, also we should add a soft-penalty for AZs with >X preempt_rate to route new allocations elsewhere automatically.
tyler: operational question: how do we measure queue_depth_inc cheaply? current metrics are expensive to compute at high cardinality.
sam: implement an approximate counter at the ingress proxy that emits delta samples every 10s (histogram) — low overhead.
infra-bot: 📈 autoscaler_eval: ran simulation on prod trace (last 24h) with hedge_pool 10% + burst_limit 4 -> 99.7% of spikes absorbed, median cost delta +3.2%.
alex: tradeoff seems acceptable for user-facing latency. we should run a week-long canary with traffic shaping on a subset of clusters.
maria: I'll own the canary. plan: roll to us-west1-a (10% traffic) with 10% hedge + burst 4, monitor p95/p99 and preempt_rate.
sam: add alert thresholds: p99 > 600ms for >5m -> rollback, preempt_rate_inc > 200% -> auto-reduce burst to 2.
linda: add an observability panel for per-AZ preempt_rate and hedged-fill usage.
alex: thanks — can you open a tiny runbook snippet for oncall to follow if canary goes sideways? include quick rollback flag and how to pin to on-demand.
maria: will do, posting runbook link when ready. tagging @tyler for infra cost sign-off. :thumbsup:
tyler: looked at infra-bot sim output, +3% cost looks fine vs latency wins. thumbs up from me.
infra-bot: ✅ canary_schedule created: start=1719001200 end=1719606000 targets=[us-west1-a] policy=hedge10-burst4
alex: perfect. thanks everyone — let's sync after 24h of canary metrics.
